title: Protocol for in vitro fluorescence assay of papain-like protease and cell-based immunofluorescence assay of coronavirus infection
protocol: Turn on the water bath to keep the temperature at 42°C.
Obtain BL21 competent cell stock and keep on ice for 20 min.
Place 50 μL of BL21 stock into a new pre-chilled 1.6 mL Eppendorf tube.
Mix cells with 3–5 μL of plasmid by tapping.
Place the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Place the tube in the water bath kept at 42°C for 40 s.
Move the reaction to ice for 2 min.
Add 300 μL LB media and incubate at 37°C with shaking at 200 rpm for 1 h.
Spread the bacterial mixture on LB plates containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin.
Inoculate a single colony in 3 mL liquid LB media containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin in 14-mL plastic round-bottom culture tubes.
Incubate step at 37°C with shaking at 250 rpm for 16–18 h.
Prepare fresh liquid LB media containing 100 μg/mL carbenicillin.
Culture at a volume of 200 and 500 mL is grown in a 1 L and 2 L flask, respectively.
Measure OD600 of the culture from step.
Re-inoculate in LB media prepared in step at OD600 = 0.01.
Incubate step at 37°C with shaking (at 170 RPM) for 3–5 h until OD600 reaches 0.6–0.7.
Prepare 1 M IPTG in ddH2O and filter through a 0.2 μm filter immediately before use.
Add IPTG to culture medium at a final concentration of 0.5 mM when the OD600 of the culture does not exceed 0.7.
Incubate the culture at 20°C for 14-18 hours while shaking at 150 RPM.
Centrifuge the culture at 6,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Pour out the supernatant after centrifugation.
Add an appropriate volume of lysis buffer to the cells.
Add DNase stock and MgCl2 stock to the cell lysate at final concentrations of 100 μg/mL and 10 mM, respectively.
Prepare lysozyme stock at a concentration of 100 mg/ml in ddH2O.
Add lysozyme stock to the cell lysate at a final concentration of 100 μg/mL.
Incubate the mixture for 30 minutes while mixing every 10 minutes.
Sonicate bacterial cells using a cell sonicator for 45 cycles (1 s ON + 1 s OFF).
Place samples on ice for 1-2 minutes after each cycle of sonication.
Repeat the sonication and cooling process 5-6 times or 10-12 times depending on volume until lysis is complete.
Centrifuge the lysed cell mixture at 4°C at 16,000 × g for 30 min.
Prepare Ni-NTA beads by adding an appropriate volume to protein purification columns and running ddH2O through them.
Add lysis buffer to the columns and let it run through twice.
Close the bottom cap of the column tightly.
Apply supernatant from centrifuged lysate to the column with closed cap and mix well.
Incubate the cell lysate with the beads at 4°C in a circular shaker for 1.5–2 h to allow binding of protein to the beads.
Let the columns stand upright for 10 min after incubation until beads settle to the bottom.
Remove the cap in the bottom of the column and let the lysate flow out of the columns.
Keep approximately 50 μL of the filtrate for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Wash the beads with 10 mL of wash buffer by letting it run through the column.
Collect approximately 50 μL of the first wash for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Repeat the washing step twice more using fresh wash buffer each time.
Elute the protein using 300–500 μL of elution buffer.
Repeat the elution step 10 times and collect the eluate.
Mix approximately 10 μL of samples with loading buffer for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Stain the gel using Coomassie blue staining solution.
Rock the stained gel at 23°C–25°C for 1–2 hours at a speed of 100 rpm.
Wash the gel using Coomassie blue de-staining solution.
Rock the washed gel at 23°C–25°C for 16–18 hours at a speed of 100 rpm.
Determine which eluates contain PLpro protein by analyzing the gel image.
Combine the protein-containing eluates.
Measure the protein concentration using a nanodrop instrument.
Concentrate the sample to an ideal volume for FPLC using a protein concentration filter.
Purify the protein sample using FPLC.
Centrifuge samples at 10,000 × g for 10 min before injecting into FPLC.
Combine eluates containing the protein from FPLC.
Measure concentration of the combined eluates using a nanodrop instrument.
Prepare sample stocks in 10% glycerol by adding 50% glycerol at 1/5 of total volume.
Concentrate step 3.y if protein concentration is too low using protein concentration filter.
Determine optimal enzyme and substrate concentration using a checkerboard assay.
Perform the enzyme assay in a 384-well plate format at the determined optimal concentrations.
Measure fluorescence signal at an excitation wavelength of 360 nm and emission wavelength of 450 nm.
Prepare the AMC substrate at a concentration of 400 μM in assay buffer.
Note: Assay buffer needs to be stored at 4°C and can be used up to 6 months.
Prepare the PLpro protein at a concentration of 20 μM in assay buffer.
Add 40 μL of assay buffer to columns 2–12, rows A-L of a 384-well plate.
Place 80 μL of the 400 μM AMC substrate into column 1, row A.
Dilute 400 μM AMC substrate in half with assay buffer to make 200 μM AMC substrate.
Place 80 μL of the 200 μM AMC substrate to column 1, rows B-L.
Move 40 μL of contents in column 1 to column 2 using multi-channel pipette.
Mix thoroughly and change tips before moving to the next dilution.
Move 40 μL of contents in column 2 to column 3.
Continue moving 40 μL of contents from each subsequent column until reaching column 11.
Discard 40 μL of the content when column 11 is reached.
Place 40 μL of 20 μM PLpro into all wells of row A.
Move 40 μL of contents from row A to row B using multi-channel pipette.
Mix thoroughly and change tips before moving to the next dilution.
Move 40 μL of contents from row B to row C.
Continue moving 40 μL of contents from each subsequent row until reaching row K.
Discard 40 μL of the content when row K is reached.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 23°C–25°C protected from light.
Measure fluorescence at 360 nm (excitation) / 450 nm (emission) using a plate reader.
Determine the optimal enzyme and substrate concentration that yields maximal un-saturated signal.
Prepare the AMC substrate in an assay buffer at a concentration 4 times the optimal concentration determined in step 4.
Prepare the PLpro enzyme in an assay buffer at a concentration 4 times the optimal concentration determined in step 4.
Prepare the compounds of interest at 2 times the target compound concentration.
Add 10 μL of AMC substrate into needed wells.
Add 10 μL of PLpro enzyme into needed wells.
Add 20 μL of compounds into needed wells.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 23°C–25°C protected from light.
Measure fluorescence at 360 nm (excitation) / 450 nm (emission) using a plate reader.
Include wells with 6-Thioguanine, a known PLpro inhibitor.
Include positive controls with AMC substrate and enzyme without any compounds.
Include negative controls with only AMC substrate.
Include positive and negative controls in at least triplicates.
Use values for positive and negative controls to calculate the Z′ factor.
Include 6-Thioguanine as a known PLpro inhibitor for assay validation.
Design a 384-well plate for high-throughput screening using PLpro enzyme assay.
Prepare the AMC substrate in an assay buffer at a concentration 4 times the optimal concentration determined previously.
Prepare the PLpro enzyme in an assay buffer at a concentration 4 times the optimal concentration determined previously.
Prepare dilutions of the test compound, ensuring that the highest concentration is twice the target final concentration.
Add 10 μL of AMC substrate into needed wells.
Add 10 μL of PLpro enzyme into needed wells.
Add 20 μL of compound dilutions into needed wells.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 23°C–25°C protected from light.
Measure fluorescence at 360 nm (excitation) / 450 nm (emission) using a plate reader.
Prepare the AMC substrate in an assay buffer at a concentration 2 times the optimal concentration determined in step 4.
Prepare the PLpro enzyme in an assay buffer at a concentration 2 times the optimal concentration determined in step 4.
Add 20 μL of AMC substrate prepared into needed wells using an automated liquid handler.
Add 20 μL of PLpro enzyme prepared into needed wells using an automated liquid handler.
Take plates for addition of compounds using a high-throughput screening machine.
Incubate the plate for 1 h at 23°C–25°C away from light.
Measure fluorescence using the plate reader.
Calculate Z′ factor for determination of assay quality.
Analyze the data for identification of hits.
Include negative and positive controls in at least triplicates.
Include 6-Thioguanine as a known PLpro inhibitor for validation of the assay condition.
Prepare Vero cells for viral infection.
Collect Vero cells by trypsinization from plates that are 80%-100% confluent.
Centrifuge collected cells for 3 min at 120 × g.
Resuspend the cells in complete Opti-PRO™ SFM containing 1× Antibiotic-Antimycotic and 4 mM L-Glutamine.
Seed 1.2 × 10^4 cells in each well of a 384-well plate using a media volume of 30 μL.
Incubate the seeded cells for 16-18 hours in a humidified 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Prepare compounds at five times the target final concentration in complete Opti-PRO™ SFM.
Add DMSO to the diluting media to maintain a constant DMSO concentration across all wells.
Add 10 μL of diluted compounds to the assigned wells.
Perform the appropriate procedure for entry into the BSL-3 facility.
Thaw a vial of virus stored in a −130°C deep freezer inside a BSL-3 facility.
Reconstitute MERS-CoV with complete Opti-PRO™ SFM at an MOI of 0.0625.
Reconstitute SARS-CoV with complete Opti-PRO™ SFM at an MOI of 0.05.
Reconstitute SARS-CoV-2 with complete Opti-PRO™ SFM at an MOI of 0.08.
Infect cells with the appropriate virus in a volume of 10 μL.
Include wells with virus only or media only as infection and no infection controls, respectively.
Incubate the plate for 24 hours in a humidified 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Dispense 17 μL of 16% paraformaldehyde solution to all wells to fix cells.
Incubate at 23°C–25°C for 30 minutes.
Wash all wells twice with 80 μL of DPBS.
Dispense 25 μL of 0.25% Triton X-100 to each well to permeabilize cells.
Incubate at 23°C–25°C for 5 minutes.
Wash all wells twice with 80 μL of DPBS.
Dispense 25 μL of primary antibody (0.25 μg/mL in 5% normal goat serum).
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Wash all wells twice with 80 μL of DPBS per well.
Dispense 25 μL of secondary antibody (0.5 μg/mL in 5% normal goat serum) containing 1 μg/mL of Hoechst 33342.
Incubate for 1 hour at 37°C protected from light.
Wash all wells twice with 80 μL of DPBS.
Fill up the wells with 50 μL DPBS.
Seal the plate with sealing film.
Proceed to image acquisition using Operetta CLS High Content Analysis System controlled by software Harmony™.
Place the plate in the HCS imaging platform and define the plate type.
Select the appropriate light source and filter.
Detect wavelength ranges from 365−465 nm for Hoechst 33342 and 495−518 nm for Alexa Fluor 488.
Choose "non-confocal" for operational mode.
Select the objective.
Adjust the focus and height of Z-stack using a well with infected Vero cells for each channel.
Confirm the brightness and select exposure time for each channel.
Test the selected parameters on one or two additional wells.
Adjust settings if necessary based on test results.
Select scan area and number of fields.
Start the image acquisition.
Open “Settings” in Harmony software.
Move to “Data Management”, then “Export Data”.
Specify “Columbus Export”.
Select data and measurements to be exported.
Specify “Export Path”.
Click “Start” to initiate export from Harmony.
Open Columbus software.
Move to the “Import” screen.
Specify “Import Type: Operetta IDX/TIF” and “Source Folder” in the “Columbus Helper Required” window.
Click “Start” to import data into Columbus.
Move to the “Image Analysis” screen in Columbus.
Select the measurement to analyze from the Data Tree.
Select one single image as representative image.
Click “Load Analysis from Disk” and “Choose File”.
Open the ∗.aas file analysis script file.
In the Define Results building block, click on Object Results.
Specify to save ALL results per object to the database.
Save all object properties calculated by the building blocks to the database.
Click “save the analysis script” when finished creating the script file.
Run a Batch Analysis.
Click “Open” and “OK”.
Adjust and test the settings for segmentation of defined objects in the Image View.
Optimize filters and input parameters of the building blocks to improve object segmentation.
Define final readout parameters of the analysis in the last building block “Define Results”.
Calculate P V using the formula P V = C N t e s t / μ C N m o c k × 100 %.
Determine the viable cell number in the treatment group as CNtest.
Determine the average viable cell number in the mock group as μCNmock.
Calculate the 50% effective concentration (EC50) using nonlinear regression with GraphPad Prism® software.
Calculate the 50% cytotoxicity concentration (CC50) using nonlinear regression with GraphPad Prism® software.
Calculate the selective index (SI) by dividing CC50 by EC50.
